comments.text: Basically, the entire middle east and North Africa (excluding non Arab countries) doesn’t have one absolute form of Arabic, there is MSA (Modern Standard Arabic) which is a formal form of Arabic, they are used in news, newspapers, official documents, broadcasts etc, Quranic Arabic (also known as classical Arabic) is a more complex one, this is the form of Arabic which hasn’t really changed since 7th century or during the Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W) era. This Arabic is used in the Holy Scripture “Quran”, classical poetry etc and colloquial Arabic, this arabic vary’s greatly each region, country. E.g Gulf Arabic is spoken in Gulf Countries such as Kuwait, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Bahrain, Qatar. These countries border Arabian Gulf, hence the name “Gulf Arabic” and many other form of Arabic
